Question:
Find the quotient when x6−3x^{6}-3 is divided by x+1x+1.

Final Answer of the CE-only Objective:
To find the quotient when x6−3x^{6}-3 is divided by x+1x+1, we can use polynomial long division. Here are the steps:
2. Divide the leading term of the dividend by the leading term of the divisor: x6x=x5\frac{x^{6}}{x}=x^{5}. Write x5x^{5} above the division bar.

3. Multiply x5x^{5} by x+1x+1: x5⋅(x+1)=x6+x5x^{5}\cdot(x+1)=x^{6}+x^{5}. Write this product under the dividend and subtract: x+1x600000−3−(x6+x5)0−x50000−3\begin{array}[]{r|rrrrrrr}x+1&x^{6}&0&0&0&0&0&-3\\ &-(x^{6}+x^{5})&&&&&&\\ \hline\cr&0&-x^{5}&0&0&0&0&-3\end{array}
4. Repeat the process with the new polynomial −x5-x^{5}: −x5x=−x4\frac{-x^{5}}{x}=-x^{4}. Write −x4-x^{4} above the division bar.
5. Multiply −x4-x^{4} by x+1x+1: −x4⋅(x+1)=−x5−x4-x^{4}\cdot(x+1)=-x^{5}-x^{4}. Write this product under the current polynomial and subtract:
